audit.whatIsWrong: Six of seven rows disagree with the packet chart, and the page is graded 'Tricky 7/10' behind a 60% win rate. whys[0] and whys[1] describe Neeko denying an escape-less champion (page renders Skill), whys[4] calls level 6 'your hardest all-in' (page renders Skill), whys[5] says 'own the mid-game pick window' (page renders Cassiopeia).
audit.why: The lane the prose describes is an early-and-mid Neeko lane that Cassiopeia reclaims by scaling; the chart rendered almost the opposite.
audit.corrected: Chart set to Neeko / Neeko / Skill / Skill / Neeko / Neeko / Cassiopeia as matched pairs, diff FAV, diffRating 4/10, carryRating 6/10, tone to the favourable colour, both difficulty lines rewritten.

audit.whatIsWrong: phases[4] treated Level 6 as neutral and phases[5]/[6] carried boilerplate about a Stormsurge spike, naming no Cassiopeia ability.
audit.why: Level 6 is Neeko's biggest spike in this specific lane precisely because Cassiopeia has no dash to leave the stun with; the row that flips is 2+ items, where Twin Fang recycles at 0.75s and out-sustains one rotation.
audit.corrected: phases[0] through phases[6] rewritten on Noxious Blast's 3.5s, Miasma's 24s, Twin Fang's 0.75s and the hidden Pop Blossom preparation.

audit.whatIsWrong: Two things. First, the biggest interaction in the lane was absent: Petrifying Gaze stuns only enemies FACING her and merely slows anyone with their back turned. Nothing on the page said so. Second, whys[4], spikes[1], mid and wants.you[1] all set up Pop Blossom 'under W-invis', and late says your escape is gone 'once W and your shields are down' — Neeko's W is a clone with no invisibility and she has no shield.
audit.why: Turning away from Petrifying Gaze converts a stun into a slow — that is the single most actionable thing a Neeko player can know here, and it is free.
audit.corrected: report[5].t now carries the facing rule; every invisibility and shield claim replaced with Inherent Glamour hiding the Pop Blossom preparation; late now states the real dash-denial, that Miasma's grounding shuts off Pop Blossom's leap.

audit.whatIsWrong: dosFull[2].d offered a 'fifteen-second invitation' after Miasma.
audit.why: Miasma is 24/22/20/18/16s — the rank-1 window is 24 seconds.
audit.corrected: Real number in dosFull[0].d and dosFull[2].d.

audit.whatIsWrong: report[8] said 'Add anti-heal early into his sustain' — right call, wrong pronoun and no named source.
audit.why: Twin Fang heals her for a percentage of the damage dealt and recycles every 0.75s; that is what the Grievous Wounds is for.
audit.corrected: Oblivion Orb named against Twin Fang.

edits.before: Levels 4-5 stay disciplined — she out-DPSes you in a sustained poison trade, so you fight in bursts, not auto-wars: E-Q in, get your value, step out before her Twin Fang (E) ramps on your poison stacks. Then Level 6 is your lane. She has no escape, so disguise as a teammate or pop a clone, channel Pop Blossom unseen, and slam E-into-R — the stun lands before her R face-stun can turn you around. That's a kill or a flash on a champ who can't dash away.

Then Level 6 is your lane. She has no escape, so disguise as a teammate — Inherent Glamour hides Pop Blossom's preparation entirely — and slam E-into-R before Petrifying Gaze can turn you around. That's a kill or a flash on a champ who can't dash away.

edits.before: You win the lane but Cassiopeia is the textbook scaler, so the longer it goes the more she reclaims. At 2+ items her stacked poison plus Twin Fang DPS out-sustains your single E-Q-R rotation, and her grounding (W) shuts off your only escape once W and your shields are down. Convert your 6-and-first-item lead into a tower or a roam-fed gold lead; don't facecheck her grounded zone in the mid-game teamfight, and let your combo delete the squishies around her rather than dueling her straight.
edits.after: You win the lane but Cassiopeia is the textbook scaler, so the longer it goes the more she reclaims. At 2+ items her stacked poison plus Twin Fang DPS out-sustains your single E-Q-R rotation, and Miasma's grounding shuts off Pop Blossom's leap outright while your 12-second E is down. Convert your 6-and-first-item lead into a tower or a roam-fed gold lead; don't facecheck her grounded zone in the mid-game teamfight, and let your combo delete the squishies around her rather than dueling her straight.

notes: The highest-value addition is the Petrifying Gaze facing rule — Riot's text says it stuns enemies in front of her that are FACING her and only slows anyone with their back turned, and nothing on the page mentioned it. It now sits in report[5].t, the Key Ability Interactions slot. Miasma's grounding genuinely denies Pop Blossom (grounded enemies cannot use Movement abilities and Pop Blossom is a leap) — that is now in late, where the page previously had a phantom 'shields'. The Shapesplitter-invisibility fabrication appeared here in four fields as on every prior matchup in this slice.
chartNote: I took six of seven rows from the packet chart but left 2+ items on Cassiopeia rather than the packet's Neeko, because whys[6], spikes[3] and late all state plainly that she out-scales — flipping that row would have meant inventing a power shift a player would trust.
